header:
Date: 2026-10-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Jenna Li (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Head of ML, Atlas Health), Tom Becker (Infra Lead), Priya Rao (Security & Compliance), Ethan Ross (SRE)
summary: POC scoping call to align on benchmark planning and harness integration. Discussed workloads (streaming vs non-streaming), customer scripts, metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens), and timeline for a 2-week pilot. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share harness and examples; Atlas to provide corpora and infra details; schedule run and compare streaming vs non-streaming results.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we have about 55 minutes, want to cover workload sizing, success criteria, and how we'll integrate the benchmark harness.
[00:12] Maya Singh: thanks lena, yes we want to be sure this POC shows realistic production traffic for our triage and summarization pipelines. Key thing for us is p95 token latency and also accuracy/regression vs our current outputs.
[00:27] Carlos Mendez: cool, real quick on our side we'll provide a harness that can run both streaming and non-streaming paths; it can replay your scripts or run synthetic load. question: do you already have prompts instrumented?
[00:40] Maya Singh: we have logs and some scripts but not a clean corpus; we can pull about 10k prompts from the last 30 days — sampling across user messages, clinician notes, and system prompts.
[00:56] Tom Becker: just to clarify, we expect up to 200 concurrent sessions during peak; the heavy ones are streaming multi-turn sessions for triage, so connection-level concurrency matters more than raw qps.
[01:12] Lena Park: good note. so for sizing we'll capture three profiles: 1) low concurrency chat-ish 2) high concurrency short completions 3) streaming multi-turn — does that map?
[01:25] Ethan Ross: yes that's what we've seen; streaming sessions maintain a websocket and send tokens as user types, we need to know how Redwood handles KV cache and long context.
[01:36] Carlos Mendez: Redwood runtime supports streaming with incremental KV cache reuse; for the harness we can emulate both incremental token append and batch non-streaming calls. One thing to call out: streaming adds overhead per connection but reduces end-user perceived latency. we'll measure end-to-end time-to-first-token and total tail latencies.
[01:55] Priya Rao: security perspective — we require data-in-transit encryption, logs forwarded to our SIEM, and audit logs stored 1 year. will Redwood's private or dedicated offering be needed?
[02:06] Lena Park: short answer: if you need customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integration plus in-controller audit, Private is the fit; Dedicated can do isolation with SLA. for the POC we can use hosted with VPC peering or a short-lived dedicated slice depending on compliance.
[02:23] Maya Singh: for benchmarking, what metrics do you recommend? we care about accuracy, p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), cost estimate per 1M tokens, and error rates. also quality regressions vs our baseline.
[02:37] Carlos Mendez: agreed — we'll capture latency percentiles, tokens/sec, concurrency, GPU utilization, and model-side memory metrics. we also include quality checks: rerun 1000 prompts through both Redwood and your baseline and compute BLEU/EM or custom scoring you provide.
[02:52] Lena Park: practical detail — the harness supports your python client scripts and k6-style load along with a small adapter for your streaming websocket tests. we'll share examples: streaming_client.py and non_stream_runner.sh.
[03:06] Tom Becker: network-wise we prefer to run the harness from a lightweight EC2 in our account and route to Redwood endpoints. is that supported?
[03:15] Carlos Mendez: yes, totally — we provide a quickstart for running the harness from your VPC; if you want end-to-end peered private control plane we can set that up but for a multi-week POC peered EC2 is fastest.
[03:28] Maya Singh: timeline ideas? we have leadership review late November so ideally results by 2026-11-03.
[03:36] Lena Park: we can do a 2-week active benchmark window. proposed schedule: week 0 (this week) share harness + corpora; week 1 run initial baseline tests (non-streaming), week 2 run streaming tests and analyze. deliverables: benchmark report + recommendation.
[03:52] Ethan Ross: curious about model variants — do you provide quantized variants or different sizes to trade cost vs latency?
[04:00] Carlos Mendez: yes, we can test multiple model variants and quant levels. we'll provide profiles for a few open models we support and Redwood-verified throughput numbers. also we can run our runtime with/without quantization to show delta in tokens/sec and p95.
[04:16] Priya Rao: audit logs — can you forward to our SumoLogic? and will the POC data be retained? we need to know retention policy for hosted endpoints.
[04:25] Lena Park: we can push logs to your SIEM for the POC; hosted retention defaults to 30 days but we can extend or configure in Dedicated/Private. we'll include retention options in the security packet we'll send.
[04:40] Maya Singh: about cost modeling — we want a clear per-token cost and also per-request overhead for streaming since sessions are long lived. can the harness estimate cost for projected monthly usage?
[04:52] Carlos Mendez: yes, the harness tracks token counts and API calls and produces an estimated cost projection given unit prices (we'll include a sample pricing spreadsheet).
[05:02] Lena Park: small gotcha — when you run streaming vs non-streaming, remember concurrency shapes batching behavior; in non-streaming heavy batching will improve tokens/sec but increases latency. we should surface tradeoffs for your SLAs.
[05:18] Tom Becker: for the technical run we'll need a short runbook: ports, sample scripts, IAM role for EC2, and expected load pattern.
[05:25] Carlos Mendez: I'll create a runbook and post it in the drive; link will be in the follow-up email.
[05:31] Maya Singh: any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:34] Lena Park: none immediate; main dependency is your prompt corpus and confirmation on whether we can spin a short-lived peered EC2 or need us to run from hosted. also security questions from Priya.
[05:44] Priya Rao: we'll send a short list of SOC2 items and a contact for legal.
[05:48] Lena Park: great. recap: Carlos shares harness + quickstart by 10/20, Atlas provides corpora + infra details by 10/22, run scheduled week of 10/26, Redwood to run streamed vs non-streamed comparison and deliver a report by 10/29. any other items?
[05:59] Maya Singh: no, that sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:02] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the runbook. bye.
references: Security packet: will attach SOC2 + retention options in follow-up
